races.title: State Senate, District 32
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Paul Lowe, Jr.
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina Senate District 32 (Forsyth County) since January 30, 2015, succeeding Earline Parmon. Listed profession is clergy, and he has served as pastor of Shiloh Baptist Church. Sits on the Senate Finance, Commerce and Insurance, and Appropriations committees.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Paul Lowe was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We could not find where Shiloh Baptist Church is located or what jobs he held before the Senate. The pages we reviewed contain no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented public stances on data centers or development, no controversies, and no foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, and his campaign site is only a short general statement about jobs, healthcare and affordable education.

cands.name: Peter Antinozzi
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 32 in 2026, based in Forsyth County. Holds a Ph.D. in biomedical sciences and a B.Sc. in chemistry and microbiology. Ran unsuccessfully in Republican primaries for Senate District 31 in 2016 and 2018. No office held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Antinozzi was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. His employment history was also not found; only his degrees are listed. We found no record of any office held. We found no documented actions on housing, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns or abortion, and no stated positions on them. His campaign site proposes tax cuts but does not address property taxes. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements, and he did not complete its candidate survey.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign site says he does not support state tax exemptions for data centers.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he would increase teacher pay and retain Opportunity Scholarships so state funding follows the student.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site lists tax cuts: no sales tax on groceries and prepared foods, a permanent 10-cent cut in the state gas tax, and lower personal income taxes. These are not property-tax proposals, so this is only a loose match for cutting taxes.
